stories.title: S1: Splash handoff fix -- readiness = Pi-core-up, not vehicle-connected (splash reaches the dashboard)
stories.completionNotes:
ROOT CAUSE was TWO coupled defects, and fixing either alone leaves the splash pinned. (1) The WIRING: eclipse-boot-state.service constructs BootStateEmitter with only statesDir+hardCapSeconds, so obdProbeFn fell to `lambda: OBD_STARTING` -- a claim that checks are IN PROGRESS, permanently false. (2) The COUPLING: that never-terminal tier GATED the handoff, capping progress at 2/3 so healthy never went true -> boot-state-poll.js never called window.close() -> splash-boot.service's OnSuccess=eclipse-dashboard.service never fired; after the 12s cap it degraded to the literal 'eclipse-obd: not ready (starting)' and held until reboot.

FIX. CORE_SERVICES_DEFAULT = eclipse-states-http + eclipse-powerwatch + boot-progress-finalize (all plain systemctl), plus the dashboard assets being installed. eclipse-obd moved to INFORMATIONAL_SERVICES_DEFAULT -- still sampled, still reported, never gating. Added OBD_NOT_PROBED ('not-probed') as the default when no tier probe is injected: same lesson as US-492's `unknown`-vs-guard-down finding, a reading NOT TAKEN must never be rendered as a state. The obdProbeFn injection seam is preserved and still non-gating, per the story's conditionalOutcome.

PAYLOAD SHAPE CHANGED -- read this before building S3/US-496 or any vehicle-slice card. `services` now carries ONLY `systemctl is-active` strings; it no longer overwrites the eclipse-obd entry with a tier verdict. The tier moved to its own top-level `obdTier` field (one fact per field, per specs/ssot-design-pattern.md). New fields: `obdTier`, `coreServices` (the gate's membership, so a consumer can see WHAT gated), `uiAssets` ('present'|'missing'). Verified by grep that the only external consumer is boot-state-poll.js, which reads healthy/degraded/degradedReason/progress only -- so nothing on the render side needed a change. No JS was touched.

JUDGEMENT CALL worth PM/Atlas review: I made missing dashboard assets a DEGRADE (holds the splash, reason 'dashboard assets not installed') rather than merely not-healthy. AC-1 names 'dashboard assets present' as part of readiness, and handing off to a dashboard that was never installed IS the A-16 blank screen -- so this converts a silent blank screen into a loud named message. A failed core unit outranks it in the one-line degradedReason (the more fundamental fault wins).

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: I did not gate on the Pi-local emitters (system-status/battery-health/light), though design §5 S1 mentions 'states server + Pi-local emitters'. Those run under the orchestrator inside eclipse-obd.service -- gating on them would smuggle the vehicle coupling straight back in through the side door. AC-1's narrower wording (states_http + dashboard assets) is the correct gate and is what I built.

TESTING NOTE for whoever writes US-499 (S6): extracted buildEmitter() so the PRODUCTION WIRING is assertable. This mattered -- no test of computeBootState in any shape could have caught this bug, because computeBootState was always correct; the defect was a dependency the entry point silently never passed. test_main_wiresTheCoreOnlyGate asserts on the emitter main() actually hands runForever. Likewise test_emitter_uiAssetProbe_readsTheRealAssetPath PERTURBS the file on disk rather than asserting a value, so it proves the probe reads the path (US-492's 'test the wiring, not the coincidence' lesson).

GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): 172 passed / 1 skipped in tests/pi/splash (22 in the rewritten boot-state module), 100 passed in tests/deploy/test_deploy_pi.py + tests/pi/ops (touched the unit file + the manifest's units), ruff clean on both touched Python files. HOST GAPS unchanged from Sprint 64: `make`, black and mypy are not installed on this Windows box -- ran ruff directly. PM: the story asks for 'Typecheck green', so please run mypy at integration time; the module gained typed params (Callable[[], bool], str|None) but was not type-checked here.

ARCHITECTURE DoD (PM Rule 10): specs/architecture.md 'F-103 Splash Subsystem' updated in-sprint -- the unit table row plus a new 'Readiness contract' subsection stating the gate membership, why eclipse-obd is excluded, and the NOT_PROBED-vs-STARTING distinction. Also corrected the deploy/eclipse-boot-state.service header, which still described the old critical-set gate, and documented why Wants= (not Requires=) eclipse-states-http is correct now that states-http is a gate member: the instrument must survive the failure it reports.

ON-PI GATE OWED -- AC-4 CANNOT be discharged from this dev box. Both validationCriteria are on-Pi: (a) bench-boot the Pi with NO car and confirm the splash reaches healthy and hands off to eclipse-dashboard rather than pinning at 'not ready (starting)'; (b) curl the boot-state after boot and confirm healthy:true, obdTier:'not-probed', uiAssets:'present'. Do (b) FIRST -- if uiAssets reads 'missing' the splash will now hold with 'dashboard assets not installed', which is the honest report of a real stale-/opt condition (exactly what US-495's force-refresh addresses), NOT a regression of this story. Note the fix takes effect on the next boot; a mid-deploy restart of eclipse-boot-state.service is enough to re-check (b) without rebooting.

Root cause (Atlas, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-pi-ui-carousel-ssot-wiring-design.md): boot_state_emitter.py assesses the eclipse-obd tier via an injected obdProbeFn, but the systemd entry point never injects one -> defaults to lambda:OBD_STARTING ('starting') forever (boot_state_emitter.py:229,301) -> healthy never true -> splash pins at 'not ready (starting)' + never hands off.

stories.title: S2: Overlay [hidden] CSS guard + /opt asset force-refresh (kill the dead overlapping DTC takeover)
stories.completionNotes:
TWO DEFECTS, ONE STORY -- and they are the same defect wearing different clothes: something was only ever ADDED and never SUBTRACTED, so a retired thing kept winning.

(1) THE CSS. Confirmed Atlas's root cause exactly, and found ONE MORE offender than the five he listed: #dtc-ribbon is a sixth, and it is the nastiest, because it also runs `animation: ribbon-pulse 2s infinite` -- an unhidden ribbon pulses a phantom alert band across every card at idle, which is a direct F-6 no-phantom violation, not just clutter. FIX is the global `[hidden] { display: none !important; }`. The !important is LOAD-BEARING, not defensive: an ID selector already outranks any plain [hidden] rule we could write, so the guard has to win on IMPORTANCE or be duplicated onto every element -- and the next overlay someone adds would ship the bug again. Documented the consequence in the CSS: an element that needs to be present-but-invisible must NOT use `hidden` (use aria-hidden + visibility). No JS touched; Iris's JS was correct throughout, and it uses `el.hidden` exclusively (grep-verified, 18 call sites).

TEST -- and this is the part worth reading. I did NOT grep the stylesheet for the guard string. tests/ui/test_dashboard_overlay_hidden_guard.py enumerates every element the SHIPPED MARKUP carries `hidden` on, then resolves the winning `display` through a miniature cascade (importance -> specificity -> source order, with a real compound-selector matcher). So it is data-driven from the artifact: an overlay added next sprint is covered the day it is added, and the guard cannot be quietly deleted. It went RED naming all six offenders and their exact winning selectors. FIDELITY LIMIT, stated in the file for US-499/S6 to pick up: only compound simple selectors are matched -- a combinator or an unresolvable pseudo-class is skipped, and skipping a `display` rule makes the test LENIENT (falsely green), not falsely red. A true CSS-cascade render is S6's job; this is the static contract S6 will exercise for real. Also pinned the inverse (each overlay STILL declares display:flex when NOT hidden) -- the cheap way to pass the guard test is to delete `display: flex`, which would centre nothing and break every overlay's layout.

(2) THE STALE /opt. Diagnosed before fixing: 'ODB2' appears NOWHERE in this repo (repo-wide grep, zero hits), so the Pi was serving a file from a generation that no longer exists in source. The mechanism: both asset steps only ever installed ON TOP of /opt and NOTHING was ever pruned, and eclipse-states-http searches `--assets-dir /opt/splash` BEFORE `/opt/dashboard` -- so one forgotten file in /opt/splash SHADOWS the real asset in /opt/dashboard permanently, and the dashboard step, which only writes to /opt/dashboard, can never dislodge it. `install -m 0644` overwriting was never the problem; the absence of deletion was.

FIX: deploy/asset-refresh.sh -> refresh_asset_dir SRC DST MANIFEST [KEEP]. Install the manifest, PRUNE everything the repo cannot vouch for (including a MANIFEST asset the source kit no longer ships -- an honest 404 beats a confident stale render), then VERIFY byte-for-byte with cmp. Both steps delegate to it. KEEP-LIST exists for one reason: /opt/splash has TWO installers (this step ships 3 served assets + version.txt; the kit's own install.sh ships the SVGs + shutdown surface). Pruning to only what THIS step installs would delete the other installer's work mid-deploy, and an A-9 skip of the kit step would then leave the Pi with NO splash -- a worse failure than the stale one being fixed. /opt/dashboard has a single installer, so no keep-list, and anything else there is pruned.

DELIBERATE POSTURE CHANGE vs A-9, PM/ATLAS PLEASE REVIEW: ABSENCE still warns-and-continues (a Pi without the UI kit ships the rest of the tier -- unchanged). A FAILED WRITE now BLOCKS the deploy (non-zero, and `set -e` aborts). Those are different facts: absence is a Pi that was never given a UI; a failed write is a deploy that BELIEVES it shipped one and did not. Continuing past the second is exactly what prints 'Deploy OK' over a stale surface and sends the operator to debug the UI instead of the deploy -- the A-16 lesson. Note the abort lands before step_restart_service, so a blocked deploy is a half-deploy; I judged a loud half-deploy better than a silent stale one, but that is the CIO's call to overrule.

WHY A LIBRARY FILE and not inline in the remote heredoc: it makes the logic ACTUALLY TESTABLE. tests/deploy/test_asset_refresh.py sources the SAME shell function that runs on the Pi (it is rsynced there by sync_tree) and drives it against temp dirs with ASSET_SUDO= -- real behaviour, not a grep of deploy-pi.sh. 7 behavioural tests incl. the shadow-prune, the keep-list, A-9 absence, and a failed write (the `install` binary shimmed to a no-op through PATH, so the production path is untouched and only the system tool underneath is neutered). Plus 4 WIRING tests on deploy-pi.sh's real step bodies -- last story's lesson, one story old: a correct routine nobody calls is worth nothing, and no test of the routine can tell you it is not called.

CHECKED AND CLEAN, no action needed: the SPLASH kit does not have the same CSS defect (#degraded-msg / #amber-ring declare no `display`, so the UA [hidden] rule applies unopposed) -- so no TD filed. carousel.js reads NO element geometry anywhere (grepped getBoundingClientRect/offset*/client*), so hiding six previously-always-rendered elements cannot perturb layout math.

GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): tests/ui 200 passed (8 new); tests/deploy 325 passed / 1 skipped (11 new, incl. the full deploy-pi.sh bash smoke test that forks ~10 dry-run invocations); `bash -n` clean on both shell files; ruff clean on both new test files. Also ran `bash deploy/deploy-pi.sh --dry-run` and read the two asset steps' output to confirm the wiring renders the right SRC/DST/manifest/keep-list. HOST GAPS unchanged (Sprint 64/65): make, black, mypy absent on this Windows box -- ran ruff directly. PM: story asks 'Typecheck green'; the only Python I added is test files, but please run mypy at integration time.

ARCHITECTURE DoD (PM Rule 10) met in-sprint: specs/architecture.md F-092 section gained (a) a 'Surface invariant: hidden means NOT RENDERED' subsection explaining why the !important is load-bearing, and (b) an '/opt asset-ownership contract' subsection with the manifest/keep-list table, the search-order shadowing hazard, and the A-9 posture change.

ON-PI GATE OWED -- AC-4 CANNOT be discharged from this dev box, all three validationCriteria are on-Pi. Order matters: run the DEPLOY first and READ ITS OUTPUT -- the refresh now PRINTS every pruned file. Those 'pruned stale asset X' lines ARE the diagnosis of the 25-day mystery; capture them before they scroll. Then with no DTC, load the dashboard (expect: no overlay paints, carousel clean + clickable), trigger one overlay (expect: only that one, dismissable), and check the wordmark reads 'ECLIPSE OBD-II'. NOTE ON THE WORDMARK: it is the SPLASH's #wordmark (splash-pi/index.html), NOT a dashboard top-bar element -- the dashboard top bar has no wordmark in this generation, which is itself corroboration that the Pi is rendering a retired generation. If the wordmark still reads 'ODB2' AFTER a deploy whose output shows no prune and a clean verify, then the stale copy is NOT in /opt and the next place to look is the chromium kiosk profile cache (states_http already sends Cache-Control: no-store, so that would be a new finding worth routing to Atlas).

stories.title: S3: Pi-local cards live + honest-gray -- Pi Health / Battery / Light always present; DTC grayed no-data
stories.completionNotes:
THREE PARTS, and the one that generated real design work was the one the AC states in five words.

(1) THE LIGHT CARD (new -- it did not exist). A pure consumer of the SAME states/light file ({lux, ts}) that already drives the auto-dim, so I made the tick resolve ONE clock (nowMs) for both the card's freshness verdict and the brightness actually applied -- otherwise the card and the screen could disagree by a poll interval about whether the feed is stale. Also DEDUPED the fetch: the tick was already fetching `light` at the end for the brightness, so a naive card would have polled the same file twice per tick at 4 Hz; the card's fetch is now reused (with a lightFetched flag so the auto-dim still works if the card slot is ever removed from the markup). TWO TILES ONLY, and the omission is the deliberate part: AMBIENT (reading + read age) and CONDITION (DARK/DIM/DAYLIGHT). I did NOT put the resulting screen-brightness percent on the card, though it was the obvious third tile: a live STOP holds the surface at FULL regardless of lux (US-484-b ch.4), so a lux-derived percent would be a number that contradicts the actual screen EXACTLY when it matters most. CONDITION is resolved against the SAME injected pi.display.autoDim luxMin/luxFull -- it is a NAME for the existing grounded thresholds, not a third set of numbers that could drift from the curve (test proves it with a config override, so the values are read and not baked in). Honest-availability recursively: a null lux (the bridge's saturation/unreadable marker), an undated payload, or a reading older than luxStaleSec grays BOTH fields with the REASON as the tile detail -- and the three reasons are DISTINCT, because "no reading ever arrived" and "readings stopped arriving" are different faults and the operator needs to know which. CONDITION grays WITH the reading because it is derived from it. No config change was needed: pi.sensors.light.enabled was already true (V0.29.15).

(2) DTC NO-DATA. The gap was narrower than it looks: the empty-available case ALREADY renders a calm gray "No stored codes", and the phantom red was S2's CSS bug (fixed). What was wrong is that an ABSENT dtc state rendered the bare word "unavailable" -- so I added noDataView(name), which names the silent instrument for the two cards whose silence is dangerous to misread (dtc: "no data -- codes not read", NEVER an all-clear; light: "no data -- light feed absent", not "dark"). Deliberately NOT applied to the other three cards -- scope fence; they keep the shipped fallback. I also preserved alertsCardView(null) === null rather than making the view report absence, because tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py:1017 pins that contract and the SHELL is the right single place to decide absence for every card.

(3) THE VEHICLE GATE -- and the hidden cost nobody costed. AC-3 names a "Live Engine Data card" that does not exist yet (Atlas puts it in Slice 2), so what is buildable now is the MECHANISM plus its one current subject. `data-vehicle-gated` cards are HIDDEN, not grayed, on an EXPLICIT source.obd.available === true. That gate is deliberately STRICTER than sourceUnavailable(), whose absent-source-block-means-available default is correct for "should I gray this tile?" and WRONG for "should I reveal a vehicle card?" -- an unreadable system-status leaves "is a car plugged in?" genuinely unknown, and this sprint has now found the same bug three stories running (US-492 guard-down banner, US-494 OBD_STARTING, here), so it fails closed to hidden and the card ships hidden for the pre-first-poll window.

JUDGEMENT CALL, PM/ATLAS PLEASE CONFIRM: I applied the gate to the LTFT card rather than deleting it. Atlas's design says "remove from carousel now"; the story's conditionalOutcome says "leave it out of the always-present set this slice ... do not fake it". Gating satisfies both readings (it is not always-present, and nothing is faked), keeps the code Slice 2 may revive, AND exercises the mechanism the Live Engine Data card will inherit -- whereas deleting it would have removed ltftTrendView + its tests for something Spool has not ruled on yet. On the bench with no car the observable is identical to the AC: no vehicle card in the carousel.

THE COST: a hidden card takes NO SLOT in the flex track, so the carousel geometry had to start counting VISIBLE cards or the gate would slide the UI to a blank frame. New pure functions visualPosition / nextVisibleIndex / nearestVisibleIndex now own translateX, the page dots (a hidden card owns no dot -- a dot navigating nowhere is the same dead affordance as the card), the swipe step-over, and the recovery when the card the operator is ON vanishes mid-session (land on the nearest visible, preferring the EARLIER -- the operator's "back", never a jump forward past cards they have not seen). goTo() now refuses a hidden target. This is real behaviour change to shipped carousel motion; it is fully node-tested but the FEEL of it is an on-Pi check.

ALSO PINNED, and worth knowing: the entire gate rests on `hidden` REMOVING the card from the flex flow, which only works because US-495's guard wins on IMPORTANCE. Adding `!important` to .card or .dot's `display` would tie importance, hand the win to the later same-specificity selector, and silently restore a gated card to the track -- the US-495 defect again, from a one-word edit. There is now a test forbidding it. NOTE for US-499/S6: the guard test only enumerates elements the MARKUP ships `hidden`; the page dots are JS-created, so the real cascade over them is unexercised.

AC-1 for the EXISTING cards needed no code -- Pi Health/Battery already gray sub-fields individually (US-400/401/429). I added a regression pin (absent power block grays only POWER while OBD/DRIVE render real values); it and the alertsCardView contract pin went green immediately, which is what a contract pin is for, not a TDD claim.

GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): 282 passed -- tests/ui 233 (33 new) + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py 49; ruff clean on both touched Python files; carousel.js parses under node (every probe-driven test requires the module, so a parse error would have failed 20+ tests). HOST GAPS unchanged (Sprints 64/65/66): make, black, mypy absent on this Windows box -- ran ruff directly; the only new Python is a test file, but PM please run mypy at integration time. NO Python SOURCE changed, so tests/pi cannot have regressed.

FIDELITY LIMIT, stated plainly: the DOM wiring is pinned by asserting on the SHIPPED tick/render/move BODIES (US-494/495 lesson -- a correct routine nobody calls is worth nothing), but that is source-text evidence, not a render. No jsdom in-repo; a true CSS-cascade/layout render is US-499/S6's job and the new visible-index geometry is the single highest-value thing for it to exercise.

ARCHITECTURE DoD (PM Rule 10) met in-sprint: specs/architecture.md F-092 gained a 'Card model: always-present vs vehicle-gated' section -- the two-tier table, why gray and hidden are different facts, the strict-gate rationale, the visible-card geometry consequence, the per-card absent-state messages, and the Light card contract incl. why brightness is not on it.

ON-PI GATE OWED -- AC-5 CANNOT be discharged from this dev box. Deploy, then on the bench with NO car: (a) swipe the whole carousel -- expect Standby, System Status, Battery, LIGHT, Alerts, and NO LTFT card and NO sixth page dot; (b) the Light card should show a real changing lux (wave a hand / cover the sensor -- it is the live TSL2591 @0x29) with CONDITION tracking DARK/DIM/DAYLIGHT; (c) Alerts should read gray 'NA -- no data -- codes not read' if the dtc state is absent, or 'No stored codes' if a real empty read happened -- either is correct, but NOTHING red; (d) count the page dots against the visible cards, since that is the one thing the new geometry could get wrong in a way no unit test sees. THEN, when the car is next connected, confirm the LTFT card APPEARS (it will read 'unavailable' -- its emitter is orphaned, which is honest and is Slice 2's item, NOT a regression of this story).

stories.title: S5: Shutdown/closeout splash -- wire splash-grace -> shutdown.html renders honestly on a real shutdown (NEW, CIO-requested)
stories.completionNotes:
THE TRAP IS REAL, AND IT IS WORSE THAN 'A BLANK 6s' -- it is a blank 6s OUT OF A 7s WINDOW. pi.powerWatch.smoothingSec is 7, so the closeout splash was invisible for essentially the entire grace period and only began to appear as the power cut. Everything around it worked: the sequencer emitted, the emitter wrote, the .path unit watched the right file, the server served the right page with the token injected, the JS read the right route and revealed the stage on time. The surface it revealed was black.

ROOT CAUSE, stated precisely because the one-line version is misleading. The kit ships ONE shutdown-only override -- `animation-direction: reverse` on the four animated classes -- under a comment saying 'the keyframes are symmetric enough that reverse just works'. Reversing DIRECTION is only half of a reversal; the running ORDER has to reverse too. The boot timeline ENDS with a fadeout DELAYED 6s, and `animation-fill-mode: both` holds the reversed animation's FIRST RELEVANT keyframe throughout that delay -- and for direction:reverse the first relevant keyframe is `to`, not `from`. `to { opacity: 0 }`. So the fill-mode that exists to prevent a flash of unstyled content was pinning the mark at zero opacity for six seconds. Note the shape of this: the bug is in the INTERACTION of three individually-correct declarations, which is why it survived a kit test suite that checks each of them.

FIX: reversed delay = T - (bootDelay + bootDuration), T = 6.5s (splash.svg's total). spin 1.5->2s, light 1.5->0.5s, fadeout 6->0s, dot 0->5.9s, s-top 0.3->5.8s, s-side 0.7->5s. No new numbers -- every value is arithmetic on splash.svg's own timings, and the test RE-DERIVES them from splash.svg rather than asserting the literals, so re-timing the boot animation re-aims the closeout instead of silently leaving it out of step. The result is an actual closeout: mark up at full opacity before the 1s PRE_ROLL reveal, light ramp dims max->low, spin unwinds, rhombi collapse, dot blinks out, all finished at 6.5s -- INSIDE the 7s grace, so the motion completes rather than being cut off mid-collapse by the power drop. After it finishes the HTML overlays (wordmark + version chip) hold the screen for the flush/poweroff tail: quiet, not blank.

THE TEST IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE STORY. I did not grep the stylesheet. tests/ui/test_shutdown_splash_render.py RESOLVES the shipped CSS -- cascade (source order + !important), comma-list animation shorthands, fill-mode/direction/delay -- and samples the mark's effective opacity on a clock, so the assertion is about what the operator SEES at second 1, 2, 3. It went RED naming every blank instant: t=[1.0 ... 6.0] of a 7.0s window, read from config, not hardcoded. One test I wrote OVER-CLAIMED and I corrected it rather than keeping a green-looking lie: 'brightness never rises' failed on the DESIGNED throb (a dip and its recovery), which reversed lands in the opening beat. The honest invariant is the envelope -- max->low endpoints, and the second half never brighter than the first. FIDELITY LIMIT, stated in the file for US-499/S6: timing functions are treated as linear between stops, so endpoints and the SIGN of a change are exact but a mid-segment value can be off; every assertion here is zero-vs-nonzero or an endpoint, which no easing in this kit can change.

DEPLOY HALF (AC-2's '/opt asset refresh'). The closeout surface was on US-495's KEEP-LIST, which sounds protective and is the opposite: a keep-listed asset is never installed, never pruned and never byte-verified by the deploy. Its only refresh path was the kit's own install.sh, which runs in the A-9 kiosk-unit step that is ALLOWED TO WARN AND SKIP (install.sh aborts outright if it cannot detect the session type or the chromium binary). So the exact stale-asset hole US-495 closed for the boot surface was still wide open for the shutdown one -- and a stale closeout only reveals itself DURING a shutdown, with nobody watching and no way to re-run it. Moved shutdown.html + shutdown-state-poll.js + splash-shutdown.svg into the manifest; both installers copy the same bytes from the same synced kit dir, so owning them costs nothing and buys the verify. I also moved splash.svg: leaving one animation asset unverified while verifying its twin is precisely the split that produced the original bug, and it is the same one-line edit. Keep-list is now version.txt ALONE, which earns its place -- the deploy GENERATES it from RELEASE_VERSION after the refresh, so the manifest cannot name it. PM/Atlas: splash.svg is the one file here that is boot-surface, not closeout; flag it if you want it reverted.

WIRING PINS (green on arrival -- contract pins, not a TDD claim, and I am not dressing them up as one). tests/pi/splash/test_shutdown_splash_wiring.py drives a REAL ShutdownSequencer grace transition into a real temp states dir, then serves the REAL kit over the REAL states_http and fetches the page at the URL extracted FROM THE SHIPPED splash-grace unit. Nothing is asserted against a literal that a rename would leave behind on both sides: the .path unit's PathExists is compared to config statesDir + SHUTDOWN_STATE_FILENAME, the JS fetch route to the same constant, and every src/data reference in shutdown.html is fetched for a real 200. This is the US-494 lesson applied one story later -- that defect was a dependency the entry point never passed, invisible to every test of the parts.

TD-069 FILED, and PM should read it before scheduling the on-Pi check. NOTHING EVER REMOVES shutdown-state. /run is tmpfs, so a cancelled grace (the common case -- that is what smoothing is FOR) leaves a phase:cancelled file for the rest of the uptime, and a PathExists trigger has no false->true transition left to fire on: the SECOND grace of a boot gets no closeout splash at all. I also suspect, but did NOT confirm and will not assert, that systemd re-triggers the unit when the service exits while the path still exists -- which on the cancel path would be a chromium restart loop. Both share one root: the state file has a write lifecycle and no clear lifecycle. The fix belongs to the producer (ShutdownSequencer / the emitter), which is the power path that bricked the Pi once (I-038), so it wants an Atlas decision, not a drive-by edit inside a render story.

GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): 745 passed / 2 skipped across tests/ui + tests/pi/splash + tests/deploy (13 new: 7 render, 8 wiring... 15 new counting the 3 rewritten deploy wiring tests); ruff clean on all three touched Python files; `bash -n deploy/deploy-pi.sh` clean; ran `bash deploy/deploy-pi.sh --dry-run` and read the splash step's own preview line to confirm the resolved manifest/keep-list (the deploy tests parse that same line, so the assertion is on what the deploy SAYS IT WOULD DO). HOST GAPS unchanged (Sprints 64/65/66): make, black and mypy are absent on this Windows box -- ran ruff directly. The only new Python is test files, but PM please run mypy at integration.

ARCHITECTURE DoD (PM Rule 10) met in-sprint: specs/architecture.md F-103 gained a 'Closeout (shutdown) surface -- the reversal contract' subsection (the two things that must reverse, why fill-mode makes skipping the second a black screen, the fits-inside-the-grace-window sizing, and what the two test files actually prove). I also CORRECTED the US-495 '/opt asset-ownership contract' table, which this change made wrong, and added the reasoning that a keep-list entry is a COST not a safety net.

ON-PI GATE OWED -- AC-3 CANNOT be discharged from this dev box; the validationCriterion is a real shutdown. Order: deploy FIRST and read the output -- the refresh now prints a 'pruned stale asset' line for anything retired in /opt/splash, and after this change that includes the closeout surface for the first time. Then trigger a real grace (pull external power with the UPS in) and WATCH THE SCREEN FOR THE FIRST 2 SECONDS -- that is where the bug lived; the mark must be UP and dimming, never black. Confirm the motion finishes before the flush rather than freezing mid-collapse. Then, per TD-069, restore power to cancel, and trigger a SECOND grace in the same boot: expect NO splash (that is the TD, not a regression of this fix), and check `journalctl -u splash-grace` for repeat starts to settle the restart-loop question one way or the other.

stories.title: S6: UI-render regression test -- catch the CSS-cascade layout class the current jsdom/palette tests miss
stories.completionNotes:
WHAT I BUILT AND WHY IT IS SHAPED THIS WAY. The three defects this sprint fixed have ONE shape: every part tested green and the COMPOSITION was broken. S1 = a dependency the systemd entry point never injected (computeBootState was always right). S2 = correct JS defeated by a stylesheet the JS cannot see. S5 = three individually-valid CSS declarations interacting to a black screen. A backstop for that class has to be compositional too, so it is TWO PROCESSES THAT CANNOT SEE EACH OTHER'S VERDICT: node runs the SHIPPED carousel.js / boot-state-poll.js against a mini-DOM and dumps the resulting attributes (it knows nothing about CSS); Python resolves the SHIPPED stylesheet over that DOM and answers the only question that matters -- does this element have a box. Neither half can launder the other's answer, which is the property the existing suites lacked.

THE LOAD-BEARING DETAIL in mini_dom.js is IDL-to-content-attribute REFLECTION: `el.hidden = true` must land as the `hidden` ATTRIBUTE, because the attribute is what the cascade selects on. A harness that stored `hidden` as a private flag would have faithfully reproduced US-495's BLIND SPOT instead of catching the bug. Everything else in the mini-DOM is scoped to what the shipped kits actually touch -- I enumerated the API surface from the source (textContent, appendChild, setAttribute, addEventListener, querySelector, classList, style.setProperty, hidden/className/id/disabled/onclick) rather than guessing; it is ~15 methods, not a jsdom clone. Timers are VIRTUAL (rounds), so carousel.js's self-rescheduling 4 Hz tick terminates and the splash's real MIN_PLAY_MS/HARD_CAP thresholds are crossed in milliseconds of wall clock.

PROVEN RED AGAINST THE REAL PRE-FIX CODE, not asserted to be (AC-2's literal discharge). test_preFixStylesheet_paintsEveryOverlayAtOnce pulls the pre-US-495 dashboard.css from git (be8084e^) and reproduces the exact defect: all six overlays paint, at idle, with NO interaction. test_preFixEmitter_pinsTheSplashOnTheBench loads the pre-US-494 emitter (13e0b84^) as a LIVE MODULE, wires it the way its own entry point did (states dir + hard cap, NO obdProbeFn -- that omission IS the bug), and the splash pins with the literal 'eclipse-obd: not ready (starting)' the CIO read off the panel. Both ran for real here (no skips). Because git history is not guaranteed (shallow clone / CI), TWO MUTATION proofs run UNCONDITIONALLY beside them -- delete the [hidden] guard rule, and strip just its `!important` -- so the backstop is self-verifying with no dependency on history, and the !important is now pinned as load-bearing, which is precisely the one-word-edit fragility US-496 flagged.

THE HARNESS FOUND A BUG IN MY OWN TEST HELPER, which is the best evidence it works. My first splash helper built the emitter BEFORE installing the fake clock, so startMono was the real boot time and elapsed() was hugely negative -- no hard cap could ever fire. Every positive test still passed (healthy does not depend on elapsed); only the pre-fix RED test caught it, by reporting the generic fallback message instead of the emitter's own. That is the whole thesis of this story in miniature: the parts passed, the composition did not, and only the end-to-end assertion saw it. The helper now installs the clock first AND RESTORES IT in a finally -- time.monotonic is global and this process shells out to node moments later; leaving a counterfeit clock under subprocess's timeout bookkeeping is how a harness starts producing its own bugs.

I ALSO CLOSED US-496's NAMED GAP: the page dots are CREATED BY JS, so test_dashboard_overlay_hidden_guard.py (which enumerates elements the MARKUP ships `hidden`) can never reach them. Here they are built by the real carousel.js and rendered through the real cascade, asserted against the visible-card geometry both ways -- bench (gated card and its dot absent) and vehicle-connected (both revealed). US-496 called the dot count 'the one thing the new geometry could get wrong in a way no unit test sees'; it is now seen. Scope note: this is one assertion pair on the harness I was already building for AC-1, not a second story.

FIDELITY LIMIT, and the mechanism that stops it being SILENT. This resolves the CASCADE, not LAYOUT: it sees 'not painted', never overflow/wrapping/pushed-off-screen. Sibling combinators are unresolved. A skipped `display` rule makes every test LENIENT -- falsely green -- which is the one failure mode a backstop must not have, so Surface.unresolvableDisplaySelectors() REPORTS any display rule behind a pseudo-class it cannot evaluate and test_harnessCanJudgeEveryDisplayRule FAILS when one appears (teach the resolver or move the rule; do not delete the test). I also added test_theRealJsActuallyRan, cheap insurance against the worst mode here: a harness that silently no-ops would make every 'nothing paints' assertion pass for the wrong reason.

TD-068 HANDLED IN-PLACE, not re-filed: the probe runner sets encoding='utf-8' explicitly, because Windows otherwise decodes the probe's stdout as cp1252 and corrupts the kit's non-ASCII copy -- a render backstop must not introduce the very fault class it exists to catch.

GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): 15 new tests pass (0 skipped -- both git-based RED proofs ran); tests/ui + tests/pi/splash = 434 passed / 1 skipped; ruff clean on both new .py files. NO PRODUCTION CODE CHANGED -- this story adds test infrastructure and documentation only, so nothing shipped to the Pi can have regressed. HOST GAPS unchanged (Sprints 64/65/66): make, black, mypy absent on this Windows box -- ran ruff directly; the new Python is a test module plus a test helper, but PM please run mypy at integration.

ARCHITECTURE DoD (PM Rule 10) met in-sprint: specs/architecture.md F-092 gained a 'Render-regression backstop -- the automated A-16 guard' subsection (the three-defect table, the two-process design, why attribute reflection is load-bearing, the RED proofs, and the stated fidelity limit), plus cross-references from the F-103 readiness contract and the US-495 surface invariant so a future dev lands on it from either defect.

NO ON-PI GATE OWED FOR THIS STORY -- and that is the point of it. Its own validationCriterion (RED pre-fix, GREEN post-fix) is discharged automatically and permanently, on this box, in CI. It does NOT retire the on-Pi checks owed by US-494/495/496/498: it covers 'does this element have a box', while the panel still owes 'does it look right and does the motion feel right'. PM: the highest-value thing to add next is a real kiosk smoke on the Pi feeding into this same harness shape.
acceptance: a render/layout regression test that asserts: [hidden] overlays are actually not-displayed (would have caught S2); only one overlay renders at a time; the splash reaches healthy/handoff on a core-up boot (would have caught S1) -- exercising the real CSS cascade, not just jsdom class presence
the test is RED against the pre-S1/S2 code and GREEN after -- proving it guards the regression
runs in the pi/UI suite; documented as the render-regression backstop
